descriptor.scene: There is no human being anywhere in this frame. EVERY figure in this picture is a factory manager of the same one design: a small blocky luminous plum-glowing mascot in a cream newsboy cap, identical to the last. THEY DIRECT AND THE MACHINES DO THE LIFTING; no manager hauls or heaves with its own body. The camera is well back inside the factory at night and THE WORK is the subject, lit warm against the dark. At the CENTRE, a new brass-and-wood rail section is being laid into the floor: a low cream machine holds the rail steady in its cradle while four or five managers stand around it at full length and small, mitten arms raised, directing it down into place. At the LEFT, two more managers stand before a half-fitted honey-wood gate across another rail, one with an arm raised toward it, judging the fit. Nearest the camera at the CENTRE-RIGHT the protagonist manager stands at full length and no taller than a third of the frame height, turned three-quarter, one mitten arm raised and extended toward the new rail, head up, weight forward. Night warmth only: the high space is dim but there is no cold blue anywhere, lit entirely by warm amber work-lamps hung low and by the managers' own plum glows pooling on the floor. Composition: new rail and its cluster centre, gate and its pair at the left, the protagonist centre-right nearest the camera; the upper left stays calm dim ceiling.
descriptor._caption: While the houses sleep, they mend the factory together. A move repeated often enough becomes a rail. A mistake repeated twice becomes a gate. A slow corner gets a shorter path. By morning the improvements are simply there, the way frost is.
negatives: cold blue or moonlit night; the night here is warm amber and plum
any figure that is not a plum-glowing mascot in a cream newsboy cap
a manager lifting, hauling or carrying the rail with its own body
a human being of any kind
